newsitem.title: UK: Grobbelaar filmed taking bribe money, court told.
newsitem.headline: Grobbelaar filmed taking bribe money, court told.

text.p: Soccer star Bruce Grobbelaar was filmed pocketing money from a business associate pretending to act for a gambling syndicate in a "sting" set up by Britain's Sun newspaper, a court heard on Wednesday.

Grobbelaar and three other defendants deny accepting or giving money to rig matches in the first case of its kind in Britain for more than 30 years. If convicted, they could be jailed for up to seven years.

Prosecutor David Calvert Smith told the court in Winchester, southern England, that the Sun's video showed the former Liverpool goalkeeper discussing a payment of 2,000 pounds ($3,300) with would-be go-between Chris Vincent.

Confronted by Sun reporters, Grobbelaar at first denied taking the money, then said: "All right. I'll put it another way. That 2,000 pounds has been put in a safe place, so I've got something against that person (Vincent)."
Vincent pretended to discuss the possibility of Grobbelaar rigging games in which he played for a second syndicate, in addition, the prosecution claims, to a syndicate based in Indonesia.

Former soccer striker John Fashanu and Malaysian businessman Heng Suan Lim are accused of being middlemen for the syndicate. Former Wimbledon goalkeeper Hans Segers is alleged to have taken money to throw games.
Vincent is the main prosecution witness at the trial, expected to last eight weeks, and Sun journalists will also appear as witnesses for the prosecution.

After being tackled by the Sun on November 8, 1994, Grobbelaar, a Zimbabwean, cancelled a trip to Zimbabwe and in the following hours there was "almost incessant telephone activity" between the defendants, Calvert Smith said.
Much of the prosecution's case rests on an analysis of their phone bills and bank accounts.

Calvert Smith said Grobbelaar -- recorded covertly by Vincent -- admitted trying to rig a total of four games, three while playing for Liverpool and another after his move to Southampton in August 1994.
But he said he found it very hard to let shots in because he was trained to keep them out. "I'm my worst enemy on that. I don't like to lose. So it's instinct," he said on one of the tapes.
Calvert Smithg said the goalkeeper claimed he did himself out of 125,000 pounds when he inadvertently made two brilliant saves in a game the betting syndicate wanted Liverpool to lose.

Grobbelaar, his speech littered with expletives, could be heard on one tape seething about a game between Liverpool and Manchester United in January 1994. United led 3-1 at one stage but the final result was a 3-3 draw.
"Do you know how much money I lost? 125,000 pounds in cash," Grobbelaar told Vincent, saying the money would have been his reward from the syndicate had Liverpool lost.
Grobbelaar said he had dived in an attempt to miss two shots, thereby allowing United to increase their lead, but the ball had hit his hand both times.

After he moved to Southampton, the syndicate told him to rig a game against Coventry. "So two minutes into the game I pushed the ball into the back of the net. And then we steamrollered them," he said, referring to the fact that Southampton won 3-1.
